title: We need a box of rice.
grammar: Count and non-count nouns; How much / How many; containers
pair_game: Point at a picture. Say “a box of rice” or “three oranges”. Your partner says if it is right. Then swap!

grammar_box.title: How much? How many?
grammar_box.tip: We can count oranges (one, two, three) but not rice or water. Use a box of / a bottle of.

questions: Do you need any rice at home?
How much water do you drink every day?
What do you usually buy at the market?
Is there any milk in your fridge?
How many oranges do you eat every week?
Do you like bread or rice more?
Are there any vegetables in your lunch today?
How much homework do you have today?
starters: Yes, we need … . / No, we do not need any rice.
I drink about … glasses of water every day.
At the market I usually buy … .
Yes, there is some milk. / No, there is not any milk.
I eat about … oranges every week.
Yes, there are … . / No, there are not any vegetables.
My favourite meal is … . There is … and … in it.
samples: How much water do you drink every day?
I drink about six glasses of water every day. In summer I drink more, maybe eight glasses.
What do you usually buy at the market?
We usually buy **a kilo of** meat, **a box of** rice and some vegetables. My mother chooses the tomatoes.
My favourite meal is palov. There is rice, meat and carrots in it. My grandmother makes the best palov!

survey.title: Class survey
survey.question: How much water do you drink every day?

game.title: Shopping bingo!
game.rules: Your teacher says a sentence. If it is true for you, cross the square. Three in a line? Say “Bingo!”
items: I eat bread with every meal.
I drink tea in the morning.
I go to the market with my mother.

mini_talk.title: My shopping list
plan: Say how much or how many
mini_talk.model: My family shops at the market near our house. We buy **a box of** rice, **a kilo of** meat and some vegetables. We also buy six **bottles of** water. My favourite meal is lagmon, because there are noodles and vegetables in it.

cando: use How much and How many correctly
talk about food with a box of / a bottle of
